title: Kenyan Eggs Benedict
community: Urban Kenya — the hotel brunch signature
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Eggs Benedict — perfectly poached eggs on toasted English muffins with grilled back bacon or avocado, topped with a silky hollandaise infused with Kenyan lemon. The hotel brunch showpiece — technical, elegant, and completely satisfying.
longDesc: Eggs Benedict is the benchmark brunch dish — the one that reveals a kitchen's technical skill instantly. Properly poached eggs, silky hollandaise that does not break, and perfectly toasted English muffins all at the same temperature simultaneously requires organisation and precision.
ingredients: 4 rashers back bacon or 1 ripe avocado — sliced
steps: Make hollandaise: whisk yolks and water in a bain-marie until thick and ribbon-like. Remove from heat. Whisk in clarified butter drop by drop. Add lemon juice and vinegar. Season. Keep warm.
Bring poaching water to a gentle simmer with vinegar. Create a gentle whirlpool.
Crack each egg into a cup. Slide gently into the water.
Poach for exactly 3 minutes for runny yolks.
Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels.
Toast muffins. Top with bacon or avocado.
Place poached egg on each muffin half.
Spoon hollandaise generously over each egg.
chefTips: Clarified butter is essential for hollandaise — whole butter causes splitting.
The bain-marie temperature is critical — whisk yolks until they leave a ribbon, no hotter.
Fresh eggs poach better — the whites hold together rather than dispersing.
commonMistakes: Broken hollandaise — butter added too fast or too hot.
Letting anything cool before plating — everything must be served simultaneously warm.
cookingScience: Hollandaise is a warm emulsion — the egg yolk lecithin emulsifies the butter fat into the aqueous yolk base. If the temperature exceeds 70°C the yolk proteins coagulate and the emulsion breaks. Clarified butter (butterfat only, no water) creates a more stable emulsion than whole butter, which can introduce excess water.
sustainabilityTips: Avocado eggs benedict — using local Kenyan avocado instead of imported back bacon — is both more sustainable and more Kenyan.
storage: Must be made and served immediately.
culturalNote: Eggs Benedict at a Nairobi hotel is both a statement of culinary ambition and a benchmark of kitchen skill. The Kenyan version — with avocado replacing bacon and sharp Kenyan lemon in the hollandaise — is a dish that confidently stakes Kenya's claim to world-class brunch culture.
